editorial:
Imagine going back to your childhood home after years of not speaking to your brother or sister. That is exactly where you find yourself with Nikola and Saša. After their mom's funeral, these two have to spend three days together cleaning out the house so they can sell it. The vibe is heavy at first, but it feels very real. You can tell they want to fix things, but they just do not know how to talk to each other as adults. Instead of having a mature conversation, they start acting like kids again, fighting over small things and bringing up old grudges that should have stayed in the past.

The acting is the best part here because the tension feels genuine. You will feel the frustration and the sadness in every scene. While the story moves a bit slow at times, it makes the emotional payoff hit harder. If you enjoy family dramas that feel like a slice of real life, you should definitely check this out. Since it is a quiet movie with a lot of detail, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the expressions, or maybe rent it on Apple TV for a cozy night in.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the siblings stop fighting and finally admit how much they hurt each other over the years. They realize that their mother's death is the only thing that could have brought them back together. Instead of leaving as strangers, they decide to keep a few special items from the house and agree to stay in each other's lives. It ends on a hopeful note with them finally acting like a supportive family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic stories about family healing.
